In this video, I compare Constellation Energy and Vistra to look at which AI power stock may be better positioned as data centers demand more reliable electricity across the United States.

Constellation has the cleaner nuclear narrative, especially with its Microsoft-backed Crane Clean Energy Center project. Vistra, on the other hand, may offer a more flexible mix of nuclear, natural gas, batteries, retail electricity, and merchant power exposure. That creates a real investor dilemma: is the better AI electricity stock the company with the strongest nuclear story, or the one with more ways to monetize power scarcity?

### Key Takeaways
- Demand for electricity for artificial intelligence data centers are driving up shares of nuclear power firms Constellation Energy and Vistra.
- Constellation plans to restart a unit of the Three Mile Island nuclear plant in Pennsylvania after striking a deal with Microsoft to use the electricity from that plant to power Microsoft's data centers.

ASK

Shares of nuclear power providers Constellation Energy ( [CEG](https://www.investopedia.com/markets/quote?tvwidgetsymbol=CEG)) and Vistra ( [VST](https://www.investopedia.com/markets/quote?tvwidgetsymbol=VST)) added to their gains of yesterday on optimism of growing demand for electricity by [artificial intelligence (AI)](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/a/artificial-intelligence-ai.asp) data centers.

Constellation Energy shares soared 8.4% Thursday when the company [announced](https://www.investopedia.com/constellation-energy-stock-jumps-on-usd1-billion-in-deals-with-federal-government-nuclear-power-8768305) it had struck a pair of deals worth more than $1 billion with the federal government's General Services Administration. One of those involves supplying more than a dozen departments in five states with nuclear energy.

Today, Constellation reported that the Treasury Department has reversed an earlier ruling and will now allow existing nuclear plants to be able to qualify for federal tax credits under the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022.1 Shares rose 3.5% in recent trading.

The company made headlines in September when it [reported](https://www.investopedia.com/constellation-energy-stock-jumps-three-mile-island-microsoft-8715895) that it would restart a unit of Pennsylvania's Three Mile Island to produce energy for Microsoft's ( [MSFT](https://www.investopedia.com/markets/quote?tvwidgetsymbol=MSFT)) data centers.

Vistra also has benefited from the Constellation news, with shares [soaring 8.6% yesterday](https://www.investopedia.com/watch-these-vistra-price-levels-as-stock-powers-higher-to-start-2025-8768614) and a further 7% today, leading [S&P 500](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/s/sp500.asp) gainers both days.

# [Constellation Energy’s earnings skyrocket as investors eye AI](https://www.ans.org/news/article-6029/constellation-energys-earnings-skyrocket-as-investors-eye-ai/)
[_Investor’s Business Daily_](https://www.investors.com/news/sp-500-nuclear-ai-demand/?src=A00444A&refcode=aflGoogleNews) reported May 10 that the first-quarter earnings of [Constellation Energy](https://www.constellation.com/), the largest operator of nuclear power plants in the United States, surged 858 percent to reach a share price of $2.78, partly as a result of promising expectations regarding demand for [artificial intelligence data centers](https://www.ans.org/news/article-5872/ai-and-data-center-growth-equal-power-demand/).

AI and data centers [play crucial roles](https://www.ans.org/news/article-5872/ai-and-data-center-growth-equal-power-demand/) in Constellation’s market forecast, which consists of the following five main points:

- AI and data center growth will drive power demand.
- Major tech companies are expected to invest $1 trillion in data centers over the next five years.
- AI data center racks could require seven times more power than traditional data center racks.

**Waiting for contracts:** Despite Constellation’s optimism and stock success, the _Investor’s Business Daily_ article suggests that industry analysts still have a wait-and-see attitude as to whether Constellation will be able to finalize the long-term contracts for adding AI data centers to its nuclear energy business.

**Meeting data center demand:** Constellation, which owns one-quarter of U.S. nuclear power reactors, is not the only energy company looking to profit from AI and data centers. [Vistra](https://vistracorp.com/) is another nuclear energy provider that has AI data centers in its growth plans. Furthermore, the expressed interest of [Chevron](https://www.chevron.com/) in AI data centers shows that plans to meet these technological demands are not restricted to the nuclear power industry. Chevron expects a surge in demand for natural gas stemming from the electricity needs of these data centers.

Wells Fargo expects that “AI data centers alone could add about 323 terawatt-hours of electricity demand by the beginning of the next decade,” According to the article. Goldman Sachs believes that “data centers will take up about 8 [percent] of total U.S. electricity consumption by 2030.”
